batches.theme: Late: tuned baseline never worse than native; switchback checks from the server

wps.notes: The pilot WP is folded in here: the pilot's pinned baseline (flow-savings-pilot-bill-12), the calendar draw (security-roles-06) and the tier rule (pages-D-11) all change verify.py, so one worktree owns verify.py, the pilot routes and the pilot pages. Expose the new fields in the API for stage 2 (per day and in the summary: claimed vs all-days totals, withheld reason, which levers a withheld day keeps, the MDI lever's month, provisional flag and rate version, carry-over share, fee basis) and list them in API_CONTRACT/types. Claims: only days whose control was actually in force claim (paused, released, failed plan, offline edge, native block do not). MDI lever priced per month with that month's tariff version, claimed once per billing month and pro rata for a sub-range, never from withheld days, provisional until the month closes; the month is re-scored at its end or after late data from inside verify.compute_day, which the nightly job already calls (scheduler.py is control-edge's: no edit there). Carry-over: chain only through claiming periods, credit native blocks' hand-over too, address HANDOFF 8.A.1 (done when the per-day ledger tracks the continuous replay within about Rs 1k over 11 days for several seeds); re-scoring that changes closed months is limited/flagged with an audit line; legacy (pre-round-6) rows flagged. Switchback result: Preliminary until the minimum days per arm, counterfactual agreement check (15 %/Rs 300), and no switchback result at a monitor-tier site (its days are recommendation_only). Tuned baseline gets the HOMER cycle-charging rule at genset sites; the perfect-foresight bound includes unserved and MDI terms and refuses time-limited solves. The metering factor (engine-savings-09) and the per-connection ledger are stage 2's. Pilot: PUT /pilot gets a request model (schemas.py) with sign-off and amendments server-owned; a second POST /pilot/start is refused; the native capture version is pinned at start and verify replays the pinned version; a later capture is recorded as an amendment (reason, old and new values, audit row). The 'a typed capture cannot claim read back by the edge device' half of flow-savings-pilot-bill-12 is sites-onboarding's (native capture form and validation). Start gates: control tier at least advisory for switchback, baseline window present with a data-completeness check and KPI list (tab A), calendar not in the past, rule checks incl. holiday closures (tab C) must pass, and the tab shows red when they fail. Calendar: a server-side draw from os entropy (secrets) stored with the calendar, not re-rollable or backdatable once locked, and only blocks painted before they began count toward the 8 weeks; 3-day blocks only where allowed, the right word for pairs, correct month labels (Nov 2026), page refreshes after 409 calendar_locked; .ics escapes text (no CRLF injection), has DTSTAMP and a file name. The Savings-page halves (amendments shown on Savings, the monitor-tier ledger title, the switchback panel) are stage 2's (features/savings); pilot success-criteria scoring (pages-D-12) is stage 2's. Every money change gets a golden test. wps.notes: Stage 2: starts from the integrated stage-1 branch, so it may touch any file; batches run in order. Batch 1 holds the engine changes that need several stage-1 WPs' code at once: multi-connection sites (high) - build_problem, the ledger, the bill rebuild and bills for every connection (the bills panel picks the connection); the metering factor per connection (VER-13: an energy and an MDI scalar fitted on two bills, tested on a held-out third, applied to both arms before pricing, a factor outside 0.97-1.03 raised as a data finding, the 2 % gate closing only on a held-out bill); the Punjab self-generation duty from the connection's province in tariff data, in build_problem and the ledger's genset cost (replacing the latitude rule); Mode B executed by the twin (per-step battery_power_w within the residual band) and used by the guard, plan_compare, the demo and verify's replay for Mode B sites; genset charging where the brand's grammar has it (Voltronic/Axpert charger source priority, Deye gen_charge): a compiled gen-charge slot, the twin executing it, and build_problem allowing a_gen per brand instead of the global GEN_CHARGE_SUPPORTED, with the farm's run hours and litres compared against today's; event re-solves for genset start/stop events, an intra-day forecast bust and an approved tariff version, as the outage events already do. Pilot go/no-go: score the stored criteria against measured KPIs, including reserve adequacy (forecasts-outages' function), constraint violations, control health, genset and cycling gates; switchback tiles show the carry-over with a correct subtitle. Audit: every mutating route writes an audit row (pilot_put, recompute, fuel_log, outage_cause, forecast refresh, set_tier_capable...), money settings with before/after values, test_audit_walk.py. Savings page: per-day lever split explaining negative days, native-block days explained inline and left out of the tuned headline, the native baseline shown (work mode, backup %, slots, capture version), daily chart ticks in rupees (no 'Rs 2k' for 1,700) and all-negative ranges, flags for withheld/not-applied/native days and a verified-only toggle, 'Diesel saved' estimated vs metered, billing-period and pilot-window options, and the Savings-page halves of stage-1 findings (pilot amendments shown, pages-D-17; the monitor-tier ledger title and no switchback, pages-D-11). wps.notes: New package for late findings: plan-row retention, telemetry read cost, tick observability and capacity, long requests and payload cost cut across files owned by several stage-1 packages (plans.py, scheduler.py, routes_sites.py, telemetry.py, battery.py, forecast.py, api.py, the shell), so they run once on the integrated stage-1 branch instead of in optimiser-plans or fleet-overview. Stage 2, in parallel with savings-ui-crosscut and tests-ci: change only the functions named in owns_files; routes_savings.py is savings-ui-crosscut's, which moves recompute onto the same jobs.py pattern (tests-and-perf-11 under pr-review-05). Plan store: retention per spec Part 3.3 (superseded plans' steps and slots kept 90 days, then only the first plan of each hour, the plan active at each step and applied plans), run from the nightly job, never removing a row verify's replays, the reports or the applied log read (test: savings and report figures equal before and after a prune); readers select the columns they use (history, current, fleet_row); plans.active_at fetches the plans covering a range once per request; indexes on plans(site_id, belief_time), plan_messages(site_id, sent_at) and acks(site_id, received_at). Back up before any schema change. Data folder: report files and site keys stored relative to the data folder and resolved through platform.data_dir(), so a moved folder still serves downloads and never silently makes a new key; reports/ goes into the backup copy beside keys/ (the key-path and key-backup halves are control-edge's engine-delivery-13 and founder-console's; build on them). Scheduler: a failing site tick writes a failed runs row, raises the plan_failed alert and still evaluates alerts, so the page's 'first plan within 15 minutes' gives way to the failure; scheduled ticks record start, end and per-site durations apart from manual re-solves (a re-solve no longer overwrites the tick's row) and log one line per tick; an overrun raises an alert; the tick stays well under the quarter at the documented sites per core (staggering or a small worker pool, DLV-09); the deterministic work limit and idle re-solve of HANDOFF 8.A.3 stay out. Requests: re-solve and resume answer 202 and run as jobs with progress (jobs.py); /now reads the header's state from indexed reads and a battery estimate stored per tick (no 30-day battery.state per poll) and re-aggregates today's day row when it is older than the last minute, so edge sites' 'today' tiles move (tests-and-perf-10); the tick reads its history window once with only the columns each forecaster needs and shares it; native_latest selects explicit columns with has_photo; one connection per request (no PRAGMA round trips per connection). Web: the shell's site switcher polls a light list carrying the state dot and last-data age instead of /fleet; GZipMiddleware(minimum_size=1000); an SVG sparkline instead of Recharts, keeping fleet-overview's cross-row scale and noise floor; ECharts registers only the charts and components used, the chunk-size warning is back on and chunk sizes go in GATES. Each change gets a test that fails without it; timings are measured and reported in the pull request, never asserted as wall-clock limits. Never run against the owner's data folder. Shared additive (append only): types/api.ts, lib/api/endpoints.ts, lib/api/keys.ts, API_CONTRACT.md, BACKEND_ASKS.md, schemas.py, new test fixture files; leave HANDOFF.md/DESIGN_LOG.md to the docs WP.

Stage 3, in parallel with parity-ui and docs. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml in both repositories, the family's shape): the backend on every push and pull request with Python 3.12 and pytest -n auto, the web repository checked out beside it with a read-only FRONTEND_READ_TOKEN (the owner adds the secret: write it in BACKEND_ASKS as an owner task), pip-audit; the frontend with tsc, vitest, build, lint and format:check and npm audit; the browser check as its own job. Deployment (the Solarlytics S0b shape): Dockerfile on python:3.12-slim-bookworm, API only, non-root, a /data volume (platform.db, companies/, keys/, reports/, backup/, logs/), HEALTHCHECK on /api/health, one uvicorn worker so one scheduler runs; .dockerignore; .env.production.example naming every GRIDLYTICS_* setting the code reads (the service-role key server-only, the founder console's 503 until its four secrets are set, Supabase only as the optional owner-applied mode with preassigned accounts, no Google, no self-signup), enforced by test_deploy_docs.py; docs/DEPLOY.md with compose and reverse-proxy notes (TLS, TRUST_PROXY, hosts and CORS); scripts/build_release.py for the GRIDLYTICS_WEB_DIST release and scripts/load_check.py (restore_backup.py is founder-console's and export_contract.py control-edge's; no fetch_tariffs/fetch_schedules scraping of NEPRA/OGRA). Web hosting: frontend/vercel.json (vite, npm ci, a deploy check before and after the build that refuses an unset or unknown VITE_AUTH_MODE or API base, an SPA rewrite of every non-asset path, a CSP whose connect-src names the API host plus the security headers, asset caching). Hygiene: both .gitignore files ignore .env, .env.*, !.env*.example, data/platform.secret, demo/*.local.md, __pycache__/, *.pyc and .pytest_cache/, and the launcher's backend-root .env.founder fallback goes; eslint 9 flat config (typescript-eslint, react-hooks exhaustive-deps, import order), prettier 3 with the Tailwind plugin and a coverage threshold from 60 % of lines, all in npm run gates and CI (fix what they flag, in parity-ui's files after parity-ui lands; a rule left off is written in BUILD_NOTES); pandas, date-fns and @radix-ui/react-popover removed and the notices' dependency lists matched; the shared sign-in stack pinned as in solarlytics-backend once both suites pass on it. Lifted code: a manifest of every module lifted from Solarlytics (path, commit, rename map) and a drift test against a read-only sibling checkout when one is present (skipped otherwise); shared onyxleaf-platform/@onyxleaf/auth packages are an owner decision, written in BACKEND_ASKS. Never change Solarlytics or Boxlytics; never push or merge: the owner opens the pull requests. Tests never use the owner's data folder.

summary: 116 late findings: 66 in 18 late batches across 12 packages, 48 duplicates in 45 groups, 2 deferred. Duplicates of original findings point at the original canonical (none of them is itself a duplicate in plan.json); late findings that repeat another late finding point at the late canonical in a batch (parity-architecture-02/05/08/09/13, performance-live-01/03/04/10/11, tests-and-perf-05). The money findings of engine-money-live are almost all repeats of round-7 originals (carry-over, MDI range, fee card, CSV, bound, gas units, tax flags, sparkline, agreement dates); their notes carry the extra evidence. New in existing packages: savings-engine (tuned baseline worse than native; switchback rule re-implemented in the browser), tariffs (fuel price before the first entry; per-lookup seeding check), telemetry-genset-battery (read transactions, CSV memory, series cap, forecast-issue size), alerts-reports (closed-alert acknowledge, re-raise after close, rule validation, channels shown live, report period/header/viewer wording), auth-security (same-second token revocation, removed members, Members wording, Supabase-mode members list and the optional web sign-in under the owner's rule, throttling, the scratch log written into the owner's data folder), founder-console (Supabase SQL ported for review only; membership-state wording), shell-nav (env.ts), savings-ui-crosscut (engine version on stored results, deleted sites, lifted wording), tests-ci (sibling contract tests, lifted guard tests, isolation, scheduler, flaky timing tests, the 7.4 contract suite, forecaster and onboarding tests) and docs (CLAUDE.md, the family docs set, Boxlytics provenance). Two new packages: storage-perf (stage 2, after every stage-1 package, parallel with savings-ui-crosscut and tests-ci) because plan retention, telemetry read cost, tick observability and capacity, long requests and payload cost cut across files of several stage-1 owners; deploy-ci (stage 3, after tests-ci, savings-ui-crosscut and storage-perf, parallel with parity-ui and docs) because CI and deployment were left out of tests-ci and nothing owns the repository shape. Accounts stay preassigned (no Google, no self-signup); Supabase stays an optional owner-applied mode as in solarlytics-backend. Deferred: parity-architecture-17 (owner decision on a family toolchain and shared UI package) and parity-architecture-22 (planned HANDOFF 8.C verification and benchmark). Some late batches have fewer than 4 ids because the package received only 2-3 related late findings and moving them would break one-owner-per-file; the late batches of stage-1 packages run after their planned batches in the same worktree.
